activity.notes: Koerikei was a ǀXam (Cape San) leader in the Sneeuberg/Camdeboo frontier. Robert Jacob Gordon's 1777 journal independently documents him as a famous chief ('capitein') and records his resistance to settler encroachment. The broader c.1770–1799 leadership/resistance interval follows the Camissa Museum synthesis and is therefore represented as approximate rather than exact.

sources.title: Robert Jacob Gordon, Second Journey, 13 November 1777
sources.citation_text: Gordon records Koerikei as a famous chief and preserves the account of his confrontation with veldwagtmeester Van der Merwe over occupation of his homeland.

sources.title: Camissa Museum — Koerikei
sources.citation_text: The museum identifies Koerikei as a ǀXam military resistance leader, gives circa 1740–1810, and summarizes an approximately thirty-year resistance from 1770 to 1799.

review_context.identity_note: Koerikei is directly attested in Robert Jacob Gordon's 1777 journal. Later sources also spell the name Korerikei. Gordon glosses the name as 'Bullet-dodger'.
